Messages.Author: Philippe Richer
Messages.Body:
Well, it has always been possible, but today I actually saw it happen for the
first time.
Someone was ousted by a 1 pool Vampire Elder Kindred Network. The guy tried to
call a vote that would save him, but ended up losing the vote with a tie (8
votes both side). His predator then played VEKN to burn the last pool the guy
had left.
Damned thing is, I was the guy's grand-predator and probably would have been
able to oust my prey on my turn. AND the vote caller.

Guys, did a oust by VEKN ever happened before in one of your games?

By the way, it was a six player game and four of 'em played Ventrues. There
was some contesting, but they each managed to get an uncontested Ventrue
Prince out as their first vamps. Weird game that was.

Bleu

Messages.Author: Tim Eijpe
Messages.Body:
>
> The question still stands though, how rare an occurance can it be to
be ousted
> by an Elder Kindred Network?
>

Well, really it is not that rare if played correctly.
Imagine this: I have an Anarch Revolt and a Ventrue Vote & Bleed deck.
The AR get's down my prey to say 4 pool, and he decides to call the vote
to burn it. I react with ELK, and vote against...if the referendum is in
his favor, I react with Kindred Coersion and reverse a number of
vampires votes to my favor. The vote is unsuccesful, and my prey then
burns the amount of pool equal to the difference in votes...

So this combination of cards can be played quite easily...also with the
Elysium, Legendary Vampire etc.

Tim
